source_caption:
22 years ago today, Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind (2004) premiered. A film that redefined the visual language of heartbreak. Directed by Michel Gondry and written by Charlie Kaufman, it remains a rare masterpiece that uses surrealism to capture the very literal feeling of losing someone you love. 

Even Sir Christopher Nolan has hailed it as one of the most original and profound love stories ever told. What Nolan specifically praises is the film's "subjective" narrative the way it maps the internal architecture of a human mind. For a director obsessed with time and memory, Nolan admires how the film uses practical effects and non-linear editing to make the abstract process of forgetting feel physically real. It doesn't just tell a story about a breakup; it forces the audience to experience the desperate, chaotic scramble to save a memory before it’s deleted forever.

source_details.synopsis: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind is a 2004 American science fiction romantic comedy-drama film directed by Michel Gondry and written by Charlie Kaufman from a story by Gondry, Kaufman, and Pierre Bismuth. It stars Jim Carrey and Kate Winslet as a couple who undergo memory erasure after they break up. Kirsten Dunst, Mark Ruffalo, Elijah Wood and Tom Wilkinson appear in supporting roles. The title of the film is a quotation from the 1717 poem Eloisa to Abelard by Alexander Pope. It uses elements of psychological drama and science fiction and a nonlinear narrative to explore the nature of memory and love.
